messages:
jess: Quick sync — thinking about an epoch-based residency tagging system for host<>GPU pages. Idea: tag allocations with an epoch id that increments on major GC/compact events. Eviction policy uses epoch age + tenant quota to avoid thrashing. Thoughts?
matt: sounds interesting. How would epoch increments be triggered? per-pool timer or on-demand compaction?
jess: prefer on-demand: compaction or explicit admin commands bump epoch. also a lightweight per-alloc counter so we can cheaply check stale vs hot
olga: concern: cross-tenant fairness. If epoch only ages, noisy tenant could starve others unless we include tenant weights
sam: can we fold this into existing residency sampler? sampler already tracks access freq, could emit epoch signals
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: residency-sampler v2 -> canary on staging at 12:30 UTC :rocket:
jess: API sketch:
```
struct resid_tag { uint64_t epoch; uint16_t tenant_id; uint8_t flags; }
// eviction score = base_cost + age_weight*(current_epoch - epoch) - tenant_quota_boost
```

cara: implementation note: storing per-alloc 10 bytes is fine, but alignment/packing matters for mmap-backed arenas. also we need compact-on-idle to reclaim fragmentation
matt: tradeoff: scanning for compaction is expensive. maybe maintain hot-set lists; compaction candidates are low-access + high-frag
olga: also need telemetry: per-tenant fragmentation metric + eviction-caused-latency spikes
sam: experiments to run: 1) synthetic multi-tenant workload with one noisy writer, 2) spike eviction latency under different epoch decay parameters
jess: ok I'll draft an RFC with API and telemetry hooks. action: jess to post RFC draft by EOD Thu. 
matt: +1
olga: +1
cara: happy to review + I'll add perf microbench harness
sam: i'll wire sampler metrics to console dashboards
infra-bot: reminder: RFC template in #eng-runtime-docs
jess: thanks all :thumbsup:
